scientific_question: Can a coupled core-to-space data-assimilation model explain and predict Earth's time-varying magnetic field with better calibrated uncertainty than static, core-only, uncoupled, and dynamo-prior baselines?
primary_estimand: Held-out difference in vector-field, secular-variation, pole-location, calibration, and source-attribution metrics under rolling-origin evaluation.
data_inventory: paleomagnetic records with separate observation model
treatment: GEODYNAMO-X with constrained physical transition, explicit external states, joint data assimilation, and uncertainty propagation.
synthetic_twin_tests: adversarial external pulse resembling core variation
falsification_rules: false attribution of external pulse to core acceleration
no held-out gain under equal data and forecast protocol
gain disappears under plausible structural sensitivity
author_scope: Research proposal only; no reconstructed field, forecast, pole trajectory, or empirical causal result is claimed.
